# Crate directories deliberately OUTSIDE the clean-room gate, each with the
# reason it is outside. Comments with '#'.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `cleanroom-paths.txt` says what is gated. Nothing said
# what the rest was, so a new crate arrived unclassified and the gate's reach
# came down to whether its name happened to start with a listed prefix — the
# `gwk-host`-passes/`gwk-pty-host`-gates coin flip. The gate now refuses to pass
# while any `crates/` directory matches neither a gated prefix nor a line here,
# so adding a crate is a decision someone writes down rather than an omission
# nobody notices.
#
# FORMAT: a path, whitespace, then a rationale. The rationale is required by the
# parser — a bare path is not a line, it is an unclassified crate, and the gate
# says so. The path must name a directory that exists: a stale line is how a
# future crate inherits a classification written for a different one, which is
# the same hole in a slower form.
#
# THE TEST TO APPLY (CLEANROOM.md rule 2, the category rule): does this code
# supervise an engine process or a PTY session — spawn, pump loop, restart
# semantics, session registry, detach/reattach routing — or emit or parse
# terminal-protocol bytes? If yes it belongs in `cleanroom-paths.txt`, at
# whatever module granularity keeps the tax off lens code. A line here is a
# claim that the answer is no.

crates/gridwork — the CLI outside `src/tui`: argument parsing, output formatting, and request/response kernel calls over the UDS. The production TUI's PTY subscription pump and detach/reattach routing are gated separately by `crates/gridwork/src/tui`; `cargo tree -p gridwork` remains asserted free of the PTY engine stack in CI.
crates/gwk — the namespace umbrella. It has no API and no code: a `lib.rs` of doc comments holding the published `gwk-*` root.
crates/gwk-cert — the conformance checker: reads a recorded event stream and replays it against the domain state machines. Consumes a file, never a process.
crates/gwk-domain — the contract: types, events, and state machines, with no I/O of any kind.
crates/gwk-kernel — the event store and its authority engine, over PostgreSQL. It supervises transactions, not engines; the only child processes anywhere near it are the ones its clients spawn.
crates/gwk-parity — the harness's PURE half only (`matrix`, `pins`, `checks`, `lib.rs`): a data model plus check functions over already-normalized input. Its engine-driving half is gated by the two `crates/gwk-parity/src/{runners,bin}` prefixes and is NOT covered by this line — see cleanroom-paths.txt.
crates/gwk-text — pure cell arithmetic: resolves text to a column count and a boundary list and stops there. It spawns nothing and parses no terminal byte.
crates/gwk-theme — the ratified surface vocabulary: the SIGNAL tokens, the mark inventory, and the pure token-to-tier resolution over both. Data and total functions only. It resolves a token to a colour SLOT NUMBER and stops there; turning a slot into bytes is the renderer's job one crate over, so nothing here emits or parses a terminal byte, and it spawns nothing.
crates/gwk-tui — the console's lens half only. It consumes frames as wire data and never links `gwk-pty` (asserted in CI). It does write to a terminal — `src/probe.rs` asks one for a cursor-position report to measure how wide it draws a mark — but asking a terminal a question is what a client does; parsing a terminal's output stream into cells is what an engine does, and nothing here does that. Its multiplexer half lands under the gated `crates/gwk-tui/src/workspace` prefix and is NOT covered by this line.
crates/gwk-context — the Context Runtime's contract vocabulary: truth stages, participation records, precedence tiers, and content digests. Types and total functions over them, with no I/O of any kind — the same category as `gwk-domain` one crate over. It resolves which of several declared inputs wins and stops there; nothing here spawns a process, holds a session, or touches a terminal byte.
